title: Rivet on the Virgin: every honor fit for the absent, short of religious worship
source_text: XLI. Denique addit nos in primis Beatissimam Virginem laudare & honorare, pro ratione donorum quae a Deo accepit maxima. Quae, inquit, si nobiscum in terris versaretur, magno nobis honori duceremus eam cum Joanne tecto excipere, ei officia omnia exhibere, quae filii debent parentibus, cum facta sit mater fratris nostri primogeniti. Reverenter etiam cum ea colloqueremur, venerabundi salutaremus, & sanctissima ejus monita exciperemus. Sed quandoquidem in terris nobiscum non versatur, nec eam videmus, nec audimus, nec infinitam, aut ubique praesentem credere debemus, quae nunc in caelo versatur, postquam sua aetate inservisset consilio Dei, ut de Patre ipsius Davide scribitur; nos omnibus iis modis & rationibus, quibus absentes jure coli possunt & glorificari, Beatissimam Virginem reveremur & colimus, dempto religionis cultu, qui ei soli tribuitur, qui ubique praesens est, & Omnipotens, & qui scrutatur corda & renes: cujus in eo voluntati obtemperamus, quum matrem Domini Beatam & benedictam inter mulieres praedicamus: idque multis nominibus; quod credidit; quod ei factum sit juxta Verbum Angeli; quod Filium Dei enixa, eum infantem diligenter curavit & lactavit, eique optimae Matris officia omnia detulit; quod eum salvatorem suum agnovit, etiam in cunis vagientem; quod ejus verbis fidem adhibuit, contradicentibus multis; quod post sanctitatis & pietatis exquisitae in tota vita hac temporali exercitia Deo gratissima pie in Domino obdormivit, & sanctissimam animam Deo reddidit; quae in caelis fruitur ea beatitudine quam suis colentibus Deus promisit, eaque in vase illo selecto, pro ratione gratiae hic acceptae, etiam gradibus gloriae, prout Deus novit, eminente. Talem nos laudibus prosequimur, ejus memoriam gratis animis celebramus, de ea reverenter loquimur, eam virtutum exemplar Christianis omnibus, maxime piis mulieribus proponimus, omnesque ad ejus imitationem, in iis quae sunt imitanda, exhortamur. Apolog. pro sanctiss. Virg. Maria lib. 2. cap. 1.
pass_a_gloss: Finally he adds that we above all praise and honor the most Blessed Virgin, according to the measure of the very great gifts which she received from God. She, he says, if she were living with us on earth, we would count it a great honor to us to receive her under our roof with John, to show her all the duties which children owe to parents, since she was made the mother of our firstborn brother. We would also speak with her reverently, greet her with veneration, and receive her most holy counsels. But since she does not live with us on earth, and we neither see her nor hear her, nor ought we to believe her infinite or everywhere present, she who now lives in heaven after she had served the counsel of God in her own generation, as is written of her father David; we revere and honor the most Blessed Virgin in all those ways and manners in which absent persons can rightly be honored and glorified, religious worship being taken away, which is given to him alone who is everywhere present, and Almighty, and who searches hearts and reins: whose will we obey in this when we proclaim the mother of the Lord blessed and blessed among women: and this on many grounds; that she believed; that it was done to her according to the Word of the Angel; that having borne the Son of God she diligently cared for him as an infant and nursed him, and rendered him all the duties of the best Mother; that she acknowledged him as her saviour, even crying in the cradle; that she gave faith to his words, while many contradicted; that after exercises of holiness and exquisite piety most pleasing to God through the whole of this temporal life she fell asleep piously in the Lord, and gave back her most holy soul to God; who in heaven enjoys that blessedness which God promised to those who worship him, that blessedness in that chosen vessel also excelling in degrees of glory, according to the measure of grace received here, as God knows. Such a one we follow with praises, we celebrate her memory with grateful minds, we speak of her reverently, we set her forth as a pattern of virtues to all Christians, especially to pious women, and we exhort all to imitate her, in those things which are to be imitated. Apology for the most holy Virgin Mary, book 2, chapter 1.
pass_b_english: Rivet ends by saying that we honor the most Blessed Virgin first of all, in proportion to the very great gifts God gave her.

"If she were living among us on earth," he writes, "we would think it a great honor to take her into our home as John did and to give her every duty that children owe their parents, since she became the mother of our firstborn brother. We would speak to her with reverence, greet her with veneration, and take her most holy counsel to heart."

"But she is not living among us on earth. We neither see nor hear her, and we must not believe that she is infinite or present everywhere. She is now in heaven, having served God's purpose in her own generation, as Scripture says of her father David. So we revere and honor the most Blessed Virgin in every way that the absent can rightly be honored and glorified, except religious worship, which belongs to him alone who is present everywhere, who is almighty, and who searches hearts and minds."

"In this we obey his will when we call the Lord's mother blessed, blessed among women, and for many reasons: she believed; it was done to her as the angel had said; after bearing the Son of God she cared for him and nursed him as a baby and gave him every service of the best of mothers; she acknowledged him as her Savior even when he was crying in the cradle; she trusted his words when many spoke against him; and after a whole earthly life spent in exercises of holiness and rare piety, most pleasing to God, she fell asleep devoutly in the Lord and gave back her most holy soul to God."

"In heaven she enjoys the blessedness God promised to those who worship him, and in that chosen vessel it stands out, as God knows, even in degrees of glory, in proportion to the grace she received here. We praise such a woman, keep her memory with grateful hearts, and speak of her with reverence. We hold her up to all Christians, and above all to devout women, as a model of the virtues, and we urge everyone to imitate her in whatever is to be imitated." (Apology for the Most Holy Virgin Mary, book 2, chapter 1.)

choices.why: The ablative absolute marks the one honor withheld from Mary while all honors due the absent are granted.
